description: webhook_deliveries.repository_id is declared as a plain uuid column with no foreign-key reference to public.repositories, so a deleted repository can leave orphaned delivery rows behind, and Postgres never enforces that repository_id actually names a real row.

required_findings.justification: repository_id uuid not null has no `references public.repositories (id)` clause, unlike every other cross-table column in this codebase's own migrations (see supabase/migrations/0001_init.sql). Without it, Postgres will not reject a repository_id that names a repository which never existed or was since deleted, and there is no ON DELETE behavior to keep the table consistent when a repository is removed.

explanation: A pure schema-integrity defect, visible entirely within the 11-line migration: the column name and every sibling migration in this repo signal that repository_id is meant to reference public.repositories, but the `references` clause (and an explicit ON DELETE behavior) is simply missing. No app code or unseen context is needed to confirm this.
